entities.summary: Pavel Peter Gojdič, was a Rusyn Basilian monk and the eparch of the Slovak Greek Catholic Eparchy of Prešov. Following the 1948 Czechoslovak coup d'état, he was arrested by the StB, the secret police of the communist regime in Czechoslovakia, and imprisoned on charges of high treason. Despite promises of immediate release if he would agree to become patriarch of the Orthodox Church in Czechoslovakia, Gojdič died at Leopoldov Prison as a prisoner of conscience in 1960. Following the 1989 Velvet Revolution, Gojdič was posthumously honoured by post-communist Czechoslovak president Václav Havel and beatified by Pope John Paul II in 2001.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in the Slovak Greek Catholic Church, Gojdič's imprisonment and subsequent death as a prisoner of conscience had significant regional impact on the Czechoslovakian dissident movement during the communist era. His beatification by Pope John Paul II in 2001 further solidified his legacy.
